incidents.classification: explore-phase data quality; corrected before any pilot analysis
incidents.description: The registered data-quality rule caps the total duration of book gaps longer than 5 s at 10 minutes. The implementation approximated that duration as (number of gaps x 5 s) and the Binance L1 builder recorded no gaps, so binance-um-btcusdt-2023-09-12 and binance-um-ethusdt-2023-09-12 (a ~20-minute bookTicker gap) were labelled AVAILABLE in results/v09/explore/data-prep-2. Fixed by summing gap durations in both builders (regression test test_long_gap_duration_is_summed_not_counted); every prepared cache is requalified under the fixed rule and failing days are replaced only by registered backups. No confirmatory or vault data were involved and no study outcome had been computed on these days.

incidents.classification: exploratory-phase rule change; confirmatory validity unaffected; disclosed with sensitivity
incidents.description: Promotion rule amended (amendment 3) after exploratory pilot results were inspected: the frozen measurement-reliability screen (Spearman-Brown of unit-level split halves >= 0.5) was replaced by a split-half consistency screen because the frozen statistic measures between-day rank stability rather than the reliability of the mean effect and blocked strong homogeneous effects. Affects which candidates are tested, not how they are decided; confirmatory data are untouched and decided under the frozen thresholds. The promotion run reports the frozen screen's decisions as a sensitivity analysis.

incidents.classification: engineering/process incident; exploratory descriptive namespace only; no output overwritten; no sealed run affected
incidents.description: Two batch-3 queues ran concurrently on 2026-10-15 08:08-08:10 local: the superseded bash queue data/v09/pilots3.sh (believed stopped on 2026-10-14; only its task wrapper had ended) began when batch 2 finished at 07:59, and the fail-closed runner lob.v09.batch was launched at 08:08 with the same 28 registered steps. Exclusive run-directory creation prevented any overwrite, the source-binding guard refused the one run whose worktree changed mid-run (generator-fit), and only the runner writes the ledger. Ledger attempts 478 and 479 are the runner's duplicate starts of generator-fit and adversarial that were refused because the bash queue already held those directories: they created nothing; results/v09/descriptive/adversarial is the bash queue's own sealed, valid run at c350b8d, not the failed attempt. 26 of 28 steps are sealed and valid (11 at a1643fb, 15 at c350b8d); generator-fit and counterexample are rerun fail-closed into -2 directories. The fills-pilot-2 run (08:02-08:08) overlapped the bash queue's lightweight descriptive steps; it is sealed and valid and its memory guard held (>= 12 GB free).

incidents.classification: final-analysis implementation defect; corrected to the registered unit definition before the sealed final analysis; no hypothesis status changes
incidents.description: After close_confirmatory (entry 618) a read-only, unsealed preview of the final analysis (final-namespace seeds, no vault input, nothing written) showed H16 using 6 of its 8 registered units. Cause: final.unit_order took the last n-1 days of each continual sequence while the registered H16 unit (continual-calibration-v09: '(instrument, k) for every earlier day') and the sealed run key the first n-1 days, so one unit per stream was dropped. Fixed to the registered definition with a regression test; the final table now also reports units_registered and units_available per hypothesis. The preview had shown statuses before the fix: H16 is ESTABLISHED with both 6 and 8 units, every other promoted hypothesis already used exactly its registered unit count, and no threshold, endpoint, direction, family or decision rule changed. Disclosed because the defect was found after confirmatory outcomes were visible.

incidents.classification: pipeline driver defect in vault data preparation; no data read, no ledger access, no substitution outside the registered order
incidents.description: Vault data preparation round 1 (results/v09/final/data-prep) prepared 32 of 36 sealed final-vault slots; 4 primaries (bybit-linear BTCUSDT and SOLUSDT 2025-08-21 and 2025-08-27) were NOT_AVAILABLE (provider HTTP 404 for the L2 file, ledger entries 641, 642, 663, 664). The driver fixed the vault dataset list once instead of re-applying the registered backup rule each round, so rounds 2-8 (data-prep-2 .. data-prep-8, sealed) re-requested the same four slots, which the data layer refused before any read; no access or attempt entry was written by those rounds. Fixed (the vault list is re-resolved through the registered backup rule every round) with a regression test; the vault design and its data are unchanged and the registered ordered backups fill the four slots.
